records.name: Álora
records.description: Álora stands on a small hill commanding the Guadalhorce valley from the north. Its Arab-origin streets climb steeply to the castle, the town's symbol, which is unusual in being used as the cemetery; the Iglesia de la Encarnación is its main church. The Desfiladero de los Gaitanes (Caminito del Rey area) and the Sierra de Huma and Sierra de Aguas are in the surroundings (Andalusian tourist board). The record point is the castle; families should know it is a working cemetery. The streets are steep, so energy is set to Medium. About 50 minutes by car from Casa de la Familia.

guide.summary: Álora: hvid by på en bakke over Guadalhorce-dalen med stejle gader op til slottet.

records.name: Antequera
records.description: Antequera is a historic town in Málaga province, about 75 minutes' drive from Casa de la Familia (Google Maps, toll roads avoided, measured by the owner 2026-10-29). Its hilltop Alcazaba fortress is the town's best-known landmark. According to the municipal tourism site (updated 2026-10-28) the Alcazaba and the Real Colegiata de Santa María are open daily 10:00-18:00 (Alcazaba last entry 17:15) and free on Tuesday afternoons from 14:00; the Alcazaba costs EUR 5 for adults and EUR 4 for children 8-12 and visitors over 65, with a EUR 8 combined ticket. The Dolmens of Antequera (Menga, Viera and El Romeral), a UNESCO World Heritage prehistoric site, are free and open Tuesday-Saturday 9:00-17:30 and Sunday 9:00-14:30; they are closed on Mondays. El Torcal de Antequera, a separate nearby nature reserve, is recorded in its own place entry. Parking, accessibility, dog policy and toilets are not yet confirmed from an official source.

guide.summary: Antequera er en historisk by i Málaga-provinsen bygget omkring Alcazaba-fæstningen på bakken, med UNESCO-dysserne i Antequera tæt ved; åbningstider og priser er bekræftet fra kommunens turistside (tjekket 29. oktober 2026).

records.name: Asador Otola

records.name: Aventura Amazonia Marbella
records.description: Aventura Amazonia Marbella is, per its own website, 500 metres from the beach and has 6 adventure circuits (MiniKids, Kids, Explorador, Jungla, Aventura and Deportivo) plus 3 initiation circuits, with 103 tree games and 24 zip lines, including what it calls the longest tree-to-tree zip line in Andalusia at 240 m. About 21 minutes by car from Casa de la Familia (Google route check, Saturday 10:00). Age and height limits vary by circuit: the park lists 6 years and 1.15 m as the minimum for one set of circuits, under-16s from 1.35 m for another, 6 years and 1.15-1.34 m for another, and a ages 3-6 option accompanied by an adult; some circuits need 1.25 m or 1.45 m. Which limit belongs to which circuit is not clear from the extract, so check the website before choosing. Prices listed: adult (from 16 years) EUR 24 low season / EUR 27 high season; ages 3-6 with an adult EUR 10 low / EUR 12 high season. High season is Easter week, July and August; opening days are in the website calendar. Hours quoted: Monday to Friday 9:30-19:30 (reservations office); weekends, holidays or same-day 10:00-18:00 (park phone). Advance booking is advised. Address: C/ Valeriano Rodríguez 2, 29604.

records.name: Benahavís
records.description: Benahavís is on the southern slope of the Serranía de Ronda, the most mountainous municipality of the western Costa del Sol, crossed by the Guadalmina, Guadaiza and Guadalmanza rivers. The village keeps traits of its Arab origin in the white-village style; the remains of the Castillo de Montemayor and a 16th-century palace are its listed monuments. Natural spots in the municipality include the Charco de las Mozas and the Embalse de la Leche (Andalusian tourist board). The Angosturas gorge on the Guadalmina is a separate candidate. About 48 minutes by car from Casa de la Familia.

guide.summary: Benahavís: hvid bjerglandsby i den mest bjergrige kommune på det vestlige Costa del Sol.

records.name: Benalmádena Pueblo
records.description: Benalmádena Pueblo is the old village of Benalmádena (Benalmádena, Málaga, España). From Casa de la Familia it is about 25 minutes by car (Google route check, Saturday 10:00). Benalmádena's official tourism site (This is Benalmádena, checked 2026-11-02): the original old village, about 300 m up the mountainside with the Mediterranean as backdrop; narrow cobbled streets, whitewashed façades with flower pots and quiet squares. Sights include Plaza de España, the Iglesia de Santo Domingo de Guzmán, the Jardines del Muro (gardens along the line of the medieval wall) and La Niña de Benalmádena, a sculpture by Jaime Pimentel. Check before visiting.

guide.summary: Benalmádena Pueblo: Benalmádenas gamle landsby, ca. 25 min i bil fra Casa de la Familia.

records.name: BIOPARC Fuengirola
records.description: BIOPARC Fuengirola is a zoo in central Fuengirola at C. Camilo José Cela, 6, y 8, 29640 Fuengirola, Málaga. From Casa de la Familia it is about 12 minutes by car (Google route check, Saturday 10:00). Its own FAQ: open every day of the year from 10:00, closing time varying by season (ticket office closes an hour earlier); the average visit is about 3 hours. Children under 3 enter free, the child rate is for ages 3-9, and the standard rate from 10; tickets bought online 24 hours ahead are €1 cheaper. The park says it is fully accessible for reduced mobility and pushchairs. There is a café inside; outside food is not allowed except for babies, children's snacks and food for intolerances. No pets (assistance dogs excepted). No own car park: the Plaza España car park opposite gives visitors a 50% discount voucher. Ticket prices were not checked.

guide.summary: BIOPARC Fuengirola: zoo i centrum af Fuengirola, ca. 12 min i bil fra Casa de la Familia.

records.name: Boliches-Gaviotas
records.description: Boliches-Gaviotas (Fuengirola). Blue Flag 2026 (used as proxy for water quality). Official tourism data (spain.info, Turespaña; undated, read 2026-11-02): Los Boliches is about 1,100 x 40 m and Las Gaviotas about 1,200 x 40 m; both are dark sand with calm water, high occupancy and urban, and both list a children's area, a sports area, toilets and showers. Las Gaviotas has the Paseo Rey de España promenade, with windsurfing and pedalo hire. Places to eat: see the linked record for La Mar Salá. Rocks: none, according to the owner's own local knowledge (2026-11-01). Municipal sources: lifeguard service daily 1 June-30 September 11:00-20:00, and on weekends and public holidays 11:00-19:00 from the weekend after 30 September until 15 October (Carta de Servicios 2026, edition 2026-05-12; the stated autumn cover ends 15 October); an adapted bathing platform at pergola 41 (Fuengirola Accesible 2025, edition 2025-03-03) with a bathing device for blind users (Carta de Servicios 2026); and one plot of 'camas elásticas' (bouncy beds/trampolines) (Carta de Servicios 2026). Fuengirola's summer bathing zone for older people (marked area, handrails, semi-submerged seats) is not on this beach but at Playa de San Francisco, the town-centre beach next to the port (municipal sources 2021-2025). Character: Developed (Danish: Tilrettelagt) - subjective assessment from the sources' description of urbanisation, not an official category. Family suitability and energy level are subjective estimates and not safety advice.

guide.summary: Boliches-Gaviotas, Fuengirola: Blåt Flag 2026. Karakter (vurdering): tilrettelagt.

guide.summary: Cabopino/Artola, Marbella: Blåt Flag 2026. Karakter (vurdering): natur.

records.name: Cádiz
records.description: Cádiz is the provincial capital, about 2 hours 30 minutes' drive from Casa de la Familia (Google Maps main figure) — long enough that it is best planned as a long day trip or an overnight stay rather than a quick excursion. The Catedral de Cádiz (Catedral de la Santa Cruz sobre el Mar) anchors the old town; its own website shows visit information but with rolling, inconsistently dated notices rather than a clear stable schedule, so current hours and price are not published here and should be reconfirmed directly. The visit is described as including a climbable clock tower (Torre del Reloj) with city views, a crypt, a small museum gallery, and a virtual-reality element. Playa de la Caleta, a sheltered, Blue Flag cove beach flanked by two historic castles (San Sebastián and Santa Catalina) with full services, is a short walk from the old town and has been a boat-mooring point since Phoenician times according to secondary sources. Parking, accessibility and the exact cathedral price have not been confirmed from an official source.

guide.summary: Cádiz, en af de ældste uafbrudt beboede byer i Vesteuropa, kombinerer katedralen og den gamle bydel med den beskyttede strand Playa de la Caleta; ca. 2 timer og 30 minutters kørsel fra Casa de la Familia (Google Maps' hovedtal), så den passer bedst til en lang dagstur eller med overnatning.

records.name: Café NOMAD
records.description: Café NOMAD is a café at Paseo Marítimo Rey de España 3 in Fuengirola. Its own website describes breakfast, brunch and lunch facing the sea, with glass doors folded back onto the promenade, parasols on the sand and "sandy feet welcome". It is open daily 9:00-15:00 according to the own website, which does not say whether this changes by season. The own website says walk-ins are always welcome; booking just means a table is waiting, which matters most at weekends and for groups. About 10 minutes by car from Casa de la Familia (Google route check, Saturday 10:00). Favourites on the own website cost about 10,90-14,20 € (price check, 2026-11-03). records.name: Café Teatro by Ocean Drive

guide.summary: Café Teatro by Ocean Drive: lounge-terrasse med levende musik og cocktails på promenaden i Fuengirola, ca. 10 min i bil, taxa eller Uber fra Casa de la Familia.

trip.schedule: Own Facebook page hours box: Friday-Sunday 12:00-00:00, Monday-Thursday closed (box marked as updated about a year ago; check before visiting).

records.name: Caminito del Rey
records.description: Caminito del Rey is a walkway fixed to the wall of the El Chorro gorge, reached via the official Centro de Recepción de Visitantes at Puerto de las Atalayas, on the Ardales side, about 65 minutes' drive from Casa de la Familia (Google Maps, toll roads avoided, measured by the owner 2026-10-29; the official site separately states 57.7 km from Málaga city). Tickets are sold mainly through online booking at caminitodelrey.info (up to 10 per purchase) or by phone, with payment due on arrival; the on-site ticket office sells only subject to availability, so advance booking should be treated as effectively required, particularly in high season. General entry is around €10, with an official guided tour around €18, a shuttle bus at €2.50 (cash only on the day) and on-site parking at €2 per day. The walk takes about 1.5 to 2 hours; the reception centre is open 8:00-14:30 and the operator advises being parked at least an hour before the booked time. Access rules are strict and relevant for families: children under 8 are not admitted at all, visitors over 8 must show an original ID document to prove their age, and anyone under 18 must be accompanied by an adult. Route length, difficulty level and dog policy are not stated on the official pages reached and should be checked before publication.

guide.summary: En dramatisk gangsti langs en kløftvæg ved Ardales; billet skal i praksis købes på forhånd online, og børn under 8 år har ikke adgang. Ca. 1 time og 5 minutters kørsel fra Casa de la Familia.

practical.label: Åbningstider
practical.text: Besøgscentret (Puerto de las Atalayas): 8:00-14:30. Shuttlebus mellem besøgscentret og stiens udgang ved El Chorro: 7:40-20:00, ca. 15-20 min. Selve turen tager ca. 1 t 30 min - 2 t den ene vej (lineær rute, ikke rundtur). Operatøren anbefaler at være parkeret mindst 1 time før det bookede tidspunkt. Sæsonændringer annonceres på den officielle side og dens Telegram-kanal.

practical.label: Pris
practical.text: Almindelig adgang ca. 10 EUR; officiel guidet tur ca. 18 EUR (grupper på op til 30, spansk/engelsk); shuttlebus 2,50 EUR (ikke med i billetten; på dagen kan den kun betales kontant til chaufføren, ikke med kort; den kan også købes online sammen med billetten); parkering 2 EUR/dag. Billetter kan også købes i billetlugen ved nordindgangen, hvis der er ledige.

trip.schedule: Visitor reception centre (Puerto de las Atalayas): 8:00-14:30. Shuttle bus between the reception centre and the walkway exit at El Chorro: 7:40-20:00, about 15-20 min. The walk itself takes about 1 h 30 min - 2 h one way (linear route, not a loop). The operator recommends being parked at least 1 hour before the booked time. Seasonal changes are announced on the official site and its Telegram channel.
trip.booking_lead_time: Online booking (caminitodelrey.info) is the primary route, limited to 10 tickets per purchase; phone booking also available (+34 952 47 05 05), payment due on arrival. Tickets at the ticket office are sold only subject to availability — online booking in advance is effectively required, especially in high season.
trip.typical_duration: About 1 h 30 min - 2 h on the walkway, plus the shuttle (15-20 min) back to the car park

records.name: Cañón de las Angosturas (Benahavís)
records.description: Cañón de las Angosturas (Benahavís) is a gorge on the Río Guadalmina near Benahavís. About 46 minutes by car from Casa de la Familia (Google route check, Saturday 10:00). The Benahavís council page on the Río Guadalmina (dated 14 June 2021) gives access hours of 10:00-20:00 with the last descent at 19:00, describes the canyon as a level 1 canyoning area where protective equipment is recommended, requires children aged 14 and under to be accompanied by an adult, and bans pets, inflatables, glass, soap and music. Prices, duration, parking and accessibility have not been checked.

guide.summary: Cañón de las Angosturas (Benahavís): en kløft langs Río Guadalmina ved Benahavís, ca. 46 min i bil fra Casa de la Familia. Åbningstider og regler er fra kommunens side (2021); øvrige oplysninger er ikke tjekket endnu.

trip.schedule: Access to the Río Guadalmina: 10:00-20:00; last departure down the canyon 19:00 (Benahavís council page dated 14 June 2021, read 2026-11-13; not stated whether this is seasonal or still current).

records.name: Carvajal
records.description: Carvajal (Fuengirola). Blue Flag 2026 (used as proxy for water quality). Official tourism data (spain.info, Turespaña; undated, read 2026-11-02): dark sand mixed with gravel and cobbles (bolos), calm water, about 450 x 25 m, high occupancy (especially at the western end), urban; showers and parasol hire are listed, and the train stops right in front of the beach. Places to eat: see the linked record for Los Marinos Paco. Rocks: a sand mixed with gravel and cobbles beach with easy access on foot, so it meets the project's beach rule (owner decision 2026-11-02: only pure rock beaches, or beaches reached by climbing down rocks, are excluded). Municipal sources (Fuengirola Carta de Servicios 2026, checked 2026-11-01): toilets, a children's area, assisted bathing and lifeguards are confirmed for the Fuengirola part of this beach. Lifeguards (Fuengirola Carta de Servicios 2026): daily 1 June-30 September 11:00-20:00; Easter week and weekends/holidays from the weekend after Easter Sunday to 31 May and from the weekend after 30 September to 15 October, 11:00-19:00. Carvajal also extends into Benalmádena, which lists its own accessibility point at Carvajal (2026). The owner confirms a mix of sand with gravel and stones (2026-11-02). Character: Mixed (Danish: Blandet) - subjective assessment from the sources' description of urbanisation, not an official category. Family suitability and energy level are subjective estimates and not safety advice.

guide.summary: Carvajal, Fuengirola: Blåt Flag 2026. Karakter (vurdering): blandet.

records.name: Castillo de Colomares
records.description: Castillo de Colomares is a monument-castle in Benalmádena (Finca la Carraca, Ctra. Costa del Sol, s/n, 29639 Benalmádena, Málaga, España). From Casa de la Familia it is about 20 minutes by car (Google route check, Saturday 10:00). Its own website (checked 2026-11-02): a monument built as a castle (Castillo Monumento Colomares). Closed on Mondays; open Tuesday-Sunday 10:00-18:00 in autumn and winter, 10:00-20:00 in spring, and 10:00-14:00 and 17:00-21:00 in summer. Tickets at the gate: adults €3.50, children and pensioners €2.50 (the page also shows €2.00 in another block; the owner chose €3.50 and €2.50 on 2026-11-11). Note from the site: the monument can only be visited from the outside. Check before visiting.

guide.summary: Castillo de Colomares: et monument i form af et slot i Benalmádena, ca. 20 min i bil fra Casa de la Familia.

practical.label: Pris
practical.text: Voksne 3,50 €, børn og pensionister 2,50 € (egen hjemmeside; en anden blok på siden viser 2,00 €, men 3,50/2,50 € er valgt). Monumentet besøges kun udefra.

records.name: Castillo-Ejido
records.description: Castillo-Ejido (Fuengirola). Blue Flag 2026 (used as proxy for water quality). Official tourism data (spain.info, Turespaña; undated, read 2026-11-02): Playa del Castillo is a large stretch of white sand, about 800 x 50 m, with moderate waves, high occupancy and a semi-urban setting close to the Castillo Sohail; it is described as suited to moragas (sardine skewers grilled in metal boats) and has a fenced dog-beach section. Toilets, showers and a sports area are listed. No restaurant on this beach has been verified yet. Rocks: none, according to the owner's own local knowledge (2026-11-01). Municipal sources (Fuengirola Carta de Servicios 2026, checked 2026-11-01): toilets, assisted bathing, adapted showers and lifeguards are confirmed for this beach; moraga boats need a Policía Local authorisation and a prior municipal fee. Lifeguards (Fuengirola Carta de Servicios 2026): daily 1 June-30 September 11:00-20:00; Easter week and weekends/holidays from the weekend after Easter Sunday to 31 May and from the weekend after 30 September to 15 October, 11:00-19:00. The charter's map legend for this beach does not list a children's area (text layer; not a confirmed absence). The Marenostrum Fuengirola open-air concert venue is part of the same area, by the castle (owner's own knowledge, 2026-11-02). Character: Mixed (Danish: Blandet) - subjective assessment from the sources' description of urbanisation, not an official category. Family suitability and energy level are subjective estimates and not safety advice.

guide.summary: Castillo-Ejido, Fuengirola: Blåt Flag 2026. Karakter (vurdering): blandet.

records.name: Castillo Sohail
records.description: Castillo Sohail is a castle above the mouth of the Río Fuengirola (C. Tartesios, s/n, 29640 Fuengirola, Málaga, España). From Casa de la Familia it is about 12 minutes by car (Google route check, Saturday 10:00). Fuengirola's official tourism portal (checked 2026-11-02): a castle on a small isolated hill 38 m above the sea at the mouth of the Río Fuengirola, on a site settled by Punic and Roman peoples; first built in the 10th-11th century, with a 12th-century Almoravid enclosure, taken by Christian troops in 1485 and partly blown up in the Napoleonic war. Restored by the town council, it also hosts events such as the Marenostrum Festival. Usual opening: Tuesday-Friday 10:00-14:00, weekends and public holidays 10:00-18:00, closed Mondays. Free entry. Check before visiting.

guide.summary: Castillo Sohail: et slot over udløbet af Río Fuengirola, ca. 12 min i bil fra Casa de la Familia.

records.name: Coín
records.description: Coín is an important town of the area at the foot of the coastal sierras. Its notable monuments are the churches of San Andrés, San Juan and Vera Cruz and the Ermita de la Fuensanta; nearby natural spots include the Alpujata woods, La Fuente, the Charco del Infierno and La Albuquera (Andalusian tourist board). The Río Grande river path near Coín is a separate candidate. About 31 minutes by car from Casa de la Familia.

records.name: Córdoba
records.description: Córdoba is about 2 hours' drive from Casa de la Familia (Google Maps main figure) — distant enough to weigh as a long day trip or overnight stay. Its Mezquita-Catedral (Mosque-Cathedral), in the Judería (Jewish quarter) area of the old town, charges €15 general admission, with reduced rates for seniors, students, and large families, free entry for under-10s and residents of the Diocese of Córdoba, and a free, unguided visit window Monday-Saturday 08:30-09:30. A separately priced night visit ('El alma de Córdoba') costs €25. The official site publishes hours through a dynamic schedule tool rather than a single fixed table; only one specific day's hours (10:00-19:00) were confirmed in this research, so a full year-round schedule should be reconfirmed before publication. If visiting in May, the Concurso de Patios Cordobeses courtyard festival (reportedly 4-17 May 2026, free entry with optional donations) opens numerous private courtyards across the old town — these dates are from secondary sources and should be confirmed at patios.cordoba.es closer to the time. Visit duration, parking and accessibility have not been confirmed from an official source.

guide.summary: Córdobas Mezquita-Catedral, en tidligere moské, der blev til katedral, midt i Judería-kvarteret, har et gratis morgenvindue mandag-lørdag ud over betalte besøg; ca. 2 timers kørsel fra Casa de la Familia (Google Maps' hovedtal).

records.name: Cosmozone Lasertag
records.description: Cosmozone Lasertag is a laser tag venue at Av. de Andalucía, 15, 29651 Las Lagunas de Mijas, Málaga. From Casa de la Familia it is about 8 minutes by car (Google route check, Saturday 10:00). The venue's terms (checked 2026-11-02): children under 6 cannot take part; players from 15 count as adults, and players under 15 must have at least one adult in their team. Games are booked online; arrive 15 minutes early for instructions, and cancellations are possible up to 48 hours before. Its own price list (checked 2026-11-02): the 1-hour 'Optimal' pack is three 15-minute laser tag games with explanation and short breaks, €18 per person Monday-Friday and €20 at weekends; the 2-hour 'Premium' pack adds 45-50 minutes in five rooms with other games (ball room, laser maze from age 9, button fight, interactive floor, laser shooting), €28/€30 per person; a 3-hour birthday pack (minimum 10 players, one drink each) is €26/€28 per person. After a pack, extra room games cost €3-4 per person per game when available, and a VIP party room is €30. Outside drinks are not allowed. Opening hours were not readable. Check with the venue before visiting.

guide.summary: Cosmozone Lasertag: lasertag i Las Lagunas, ca. 8 min i bil fra Casa de la Familia.

records.name: Cueva del Tesoro
records.description: Cueva del Tesoro is, according to the Rincón de la Victoria tourist site, one of only three caves of marine origin known in the world. Palaeolithic and Bronze Age remains and rock art were found in its galleries. About 43 minutes by car from Casa de la Familia (Google route check, Saturday 10:00). Winter season (1 October to 30 April): 10:00-13:00 and 15:00-17:00. Summer season (1 May to 30 September): 10:30-13:00 and 16:30-19:00. Closed on 24, 25 and 31 December and on 1 and 6 January. Tickets on the same page: children 0-3 free, children 4-14 EUR 4, adults 15-64 EUR 6. For safety, tickets must be booked in advance (online or by phone, 952 40 61 62). The cave is not fully accessible: most of it is low difficulty, a lift reaches the first chamber (the limit for visitors with reduced mobility), and the rest has flights of steps. Prices, hours and access are from the town's tourism page, not a cave-owned site.

records.name: Dunas de Artola

Three kinds of dunes can be seen: moving dunes with ripples by the beach, inactive dunes covered with plants further in, and fossil dunes under dense pine forest. Plants include marram grass, sea holly and sea daffodils. Visitors should keep to the marked paths, because trampling damages the dunes. Nearby are the Torre de los Ladrones (a listed watchtower), Cabopino marina and Cabopino beach, part of which is nudist. Check conditions before setting out.

records.description: El Torcal de Antequera is a karst nature reserve of eroded limestone formations, about 85 minutes' drive from Casa de la Familia (Google Maps, toll roads avoided, measured by the owner 2026-10-29). The visitor centre area sits off the Antequera–Villanueva de la Concepción road; self-guided visits on the marked Green (~45 min) and Yellow (~1h30) trails need no advance booking and are free, while small-group guided routes such as the 'Ruta de los Ammonites' (around 3 hours) or longer 5-hour routes must be booked in advance by phone or email because group sizes are kept small. The rocky, uneven terrain calls for sturdy shoes; a shuttle bus can substitute for car access to the upper car park on the busiest days. The visitor centre (Torcal Alto) is open daily from 9:30 to 17:00 or 17:30 (the park's site and the municipality differ by 30 minutes), with a restaurant, a car park and a shuttle (EUR 3 return) on days when private cars are restricted. Dogs are allowed on a lead. records.name: Gibraltar
records.description: Gibraltar is reached from Casa de la Familia in about 1 hour 40 minutes' drive (Google Maps main figure, to Gibraltar town centre including roughly 10 minutes inside Gibraltar; the land border at La Línea de la Concepción comes earlier on the route), making it a British Overseas Territory rather than Spain. Since 15 July 2026, the border has been genuinely easy to cross: a UK-EU-Spain treaty was provisionally implemented that day, the frontier gates and physical barrier were removed, and the Government of Gibraltar describes the result as a fluid frontier without routine immigration controls — confirmed directly from the official government press release. Secondary reporting (not confirmed on that same official page) describes Schengen passport checks for non-EU arrivals as having moved to Gibraltar's airport and port instead, with most goods customs-cleared at EU offices in Spain before entering Gibraltar; the official release itself flagged 'teething issues' during initial implementation, so visitors should expect some residual friction even though the old queueing fence is gone. The Upper Rock Nature Reserve, run by the Gibraltar government, charges £30 for adults and £22 for children 5-11 (under-5s free, with proof of age required), with winter hours 09:00-18:15 and summer hours 09:30-19:15; it includes St Michael's Cave, the Great Siege Tunnels, and the Barbary macaques — described as the only wild primate population in Europe — near the Ape's Den. Importantly, the Rock's famous cable car is currently closed for a full refurbishment and not expected to reopen until 2027 at the earliest, so visitors must currently reach the upper reserve by road/shuttle rather than by cable car. Car queues at the frontier, which were long and unpredictable before the treaty, should now be much reduced given the barrier's removal, though Gibraltar's town centre remains compact and parking in La Línea with a walk across may still be convenient. Currency: the Gibraltar pound is pegged 1:1 to sterling and sterling is accepted at face value, but euro acceptance is inconsistent across sources — carrying sterling/GIP is the safer recommendation pending clearer confirmation.

guide.summary: Gibraltar, britisk oversøisk territorium nået over landegrænsen fra La Línea, byder på berberaber og vid udsigt over strædet i Upper Rock Nature Reserve samt shopping på Main Street. Klippens kendte svævebane er lukket for renovering til mindst 2027.

records.name: Granada
records.description: Granada is about 1 hour 50 minutes' drive from Casa de la Familia (Google Maps main figure). Per owner decision, the Alhambra is treated as part of this record rather than a separate one. The Alhambra's gardens, Generalife and Alcazaba are open daily (08:30-18:00 winter, 08:30-20:00 summer), while the Nasrid Palaces use timed entry capped at 300 visitors per 30-minute slot — a general visit takes around 3 hours. Tickets (General Day Tour €22.27, or the cheaper Andalusian Monuments Visit at €8.48) are sold via the official site, by phone, at ticket machines, or same-day at the office subject to availability; secondary sources consistently (though not officially confirmed) describe tickets as released roughly 3 months ahead and liable to sell out in high season, so advance booking is strongly recommended. Visitors 14 and older without an accompanying adult must carry ID; under-14s must be accompanied. The official site recommends flat, closed footwear for cobblestones, uneven steps and bare-earth sections. Beyond the Alhambra, the Albaicín's free Mirador de San Nicolás viewpoint offers a well-known view back toward the Alhambra with the Sierra Nevada behind it, though it gets crowded, especially at sunset. The official FAQ lists a guarded car park with 360 spaces, a wheelchair itinerary (with steps and uneven areas elsewhere), toilets at the ticket office and inside the complex, and no dogs except guide and assistance dogs. On-site food has not been confirmed.

records.name: Jerez de la Frontera
records.description: Jerez de la Frontera is a historic Cádiz-province city, about 2 hours 20 minutes' drive from Casa de la Familia (Google Maps main figure). The Alcázar de Jerez, an 11th-century Moorish fortress, anchors the old town; a camera obscura inside carries an additional fee. Its official opening hours are now confirmed: daily 08:30-14:30 from January to June and October to December, and with longer weekday hours (08:30-17:30) from July to September; current admission price is not confirmed (the only official figure found is a 2020, pre-pandemic document, too old to publish as current). Jerez is known as 'the world capital of sherry', home to historic bodegas including González Byass (founded 1835, maker of Tío Pepe), Williams & Humbert (1877) and Grupo Garvey (1780); Brandy de Jerez can only be produced within the 'Sherry Triangle' of Jerez, El Puerto de Santa María and Sanlúcar de Barrameda. The city also has a flamenco museum (Centro Andaluz de Flamenco) and is the historic home of the Royal Andalusian School of Equestrian Art and the Carthusian horse breed. A González Byass bodega tour (around 90 minutes, ending in a wine tasting) is commonly sold through third-party booking sites at roughly €17.50-19 per person; no venue-specific minimum age for the tasting was found, but per editor decision this needs no further chasing — Spain's standard legal drinking age of 18 governs the tasting regardless of how the tour itself is marketed.

records.name: La Butibamba
records.description: La Butibamba (Mijas). Not on the ADEAC Blue Flag 2026 list, so no indirect water-quality indication. Official tourism data (spain.info, Turespaña; undated, read 2026-11-02): about 1,300 x 20 m, calm water, high occupancy, urban, joined to La Cala beach by the same shore; showers and parasol/sunbed hire are listed. Places to eat: see the linked records for Chiringuito Cristóbal and Chiringuito Los Moreno. Rocks: none - it is a stone beach, not a rocky one (owner's own knowledge, 2026-11-01). Municipal sources (Mijas 2026, checked 2026-11-01): lifeguards daily 1 June-30 September 11:00-20:00 (local press: two towers at this beach and weekend cover in May and October); no assisted-bathing point at this beach (nearest: La Cala). records.name: Las Alpujarras
records.description: Las Alpujarras is a region of white villages in the valleys south of Sierra Nevada, known for a relaxed, unhurried pace compared to much of the rest of Andalusia — not a single point, but per editor decision this record anchors on Pampaneira, the lowest and most accessible of the three well-known Poqueira-gorge villages (Pampaneira, Bubión, Capileira), reached via a narrow, winding mountain road about 2 hours 20 minutes' drive from Casa de la Familia (route-checked), chosen over the higher village of Capileira for its broader, easier-access appeal. Pampaneira keeps its Moorish-era heritage, with narrow streets and alleys, inviting squares, and traditional houses decorated with Alpujarra-style textile banners, per Spain's official tourism site; the nearby Buddhist monastery and meditation retreat O Sel Ling is a notable sight. The long-distance GR-7 trail passes through, with a roughly 6 km stretch connecting Pampaneira to Capileira; the GR-240 (Sulayr) ring trail also crosses the area, though the full Sulayr circuit is considered demanding and sources recommend day-walk segments rather than the whole route for casual visitors. Two claims should NOT be assumed without further confirmation: the region's famous cured-ham (jamón) tradition is tied to Trevélez, not Pampaneira, and Pampaneira's own reputation for craft/textile shops is repeated across secondary sources but not yet confirmed from an official page. Whether Mulhacén hiking routes start precisely at Pampaneira was not confirmed.

guide.summary: Las Alpujarras er en bjergegn med hvide landsbyer syd for Sierra Nevada og et tydeligt roligere tempo end meget af Andalusien; stedet tager udgangspunkt i Pampaneira, den laveste og lettest tilgængelige af landsbyerne i Poqueira-kløften.

records.name: Málaga
records.description: Málaga is the provincial capital, about 47 minutes' drive from Casa de la Familia (Google Maps, toll roads avoided, measured by the owner 2026-10-29), or about 46 minutes by Cercanías C1 train from Fuengirola station, which is 16 minutes' drive from the house and avoids city-centre parking. The historic centre is anchored by the Catedral de la Encarnación (Calle Molina Lario 9), open with seasonal hours (shorter on Sundays) and priced at €10 for a general ticket including an audioguide, with reduced rates for teenagers, students and seniors; a rooftop ('Cubiertas') tour and an organ tour are offered separately; the rooftop tour climbs a narrow spiral staircase of about 200 steps and the cathedral's site says it is not suitable for visitors who cannot manage stairs. A short walk away, the Alcazaba hilltop fortress (and the adjoining Gibralfaro castle) is open daily with a combined ticket around €10 and free entry every Sunday afternoon; expect stairs and uneven, sloping paths on the fortress grounds. Accessibility, parking, and dog policy at these venues have not yet been confirmed from an official source and should be checked before a visit with mobility needs or pets. More sights in the centre, chosen by the owner for this record (2026-11-02): the Roman theatre on Calle Alcazabilla at the foot of the Alcazaba; the Museo Picasso Málaga, open every day from 10:00 (own site); the Museo Interactivo de la Música (MIMMA, Calle Beatas 15), a hands-on museum where visitors may play instruments - winter hours 7 September-24 June Monday 10:00-16:00 and Tuesday-Sunday 10:00-19:00, adults €6, reduced €4, free under 6 with an adult (own site); the Parque de Málaga, a landscaped park along the port; Muelle Uno, the port promenade with shops and restaurants; the Mercado de Atarazanas (separate record); and, west of the centre, the Museo del Automóvil y la Moda, with classic cars and haute couture (own site). Malagueta beach (separate record) is within about a kilometre of the Alcazaba and Gibralfaro (spain.info).

records.name: Nerja
records.description: Nerja is a coastal town east of Málaga, about 1 hour 15 minutes' drive from Casa de la Familia (Google Maps main figure). Its best-known sight, the Balcón de Europa, is a free public viewpoint on the site of a former medieval fortress, with two old cannon emplacements, a small chapel, a bronze statue of King Alfonso XII, and a café-lined promenade, flanked by Playa Calahonda and Playa Caletilla; it is said to take its name from an 1885 royal visit, though this is a widely repeated local story rather than an officially documented fact. A short drive away at Maro, the Cuevas de Nerja show caves are open 09:15-16:30 in the standard period and 09:15-17:30 in peak season (June-September, Christmas, bridge holidays, Holy Week), closed on a short list of public holidays; exact current ticket prices were not confirmed from the official page in this pass, but online booking is available and described as cheaper than paying at the gate. Nerja neighbours Frigiliana, a separate existing record, a short drive away on a winding road. Parking near the Balcón itself is reported as difficult (not officially confirmed), and accessibility has not been assessed. Suggested order (editor decision 2026-10-30): start at the Cuevas de Nerja, which is where the Google Maps route ends and the nearest natural starting point, then the Balcón de Europa and the nearby beach.

guide.summary: En dag omkring Nerja: start ved Cuevas de Nerja i Maro, fortsæt til det gratis udsigtspunkt Balcón de Europa i byen og slut på stranden tæt ved; ca. 1 time og 15 minutters kørsel fra Casa de la Familia (Google Maps' hovedtal, til grotterne).

records.name: Noniná
records.description: Noniná (also 'Noniná puerto de Fuengirola') is a flamenco bar at C. Puerto, 29640 Fuengirola, Málaga. From Casa de la Familia it is about 15 minutes by car, taxi or Uber (Google route check, Saturday 10:00; evening traffic differs). Its own Facebook page (checked 2026-11-02) describes it as a bar with flamenco, slogan 'Tú eres parte del espectáculo', phone +34 685 39 43 25 (also WhatsApp). Recent posts advertise a 'Día de la Fiesta Flamenca' with arroz caldoso and live music on 7 October from 15:00, and images refer to the Feria de Fuengirola 2026, so the venue may be tied to the October fair; regular opening days, hours and prices are not given. records.name: Ojén
records.description: Ojén lies between Sierra Alpujata and Sierra Blanca behind Marbella. The village, surrounded by vegetable gardens, keeps its stepped houses on the slope from its Arab origins and is regarded as one of the prettiest villages in the province; remains of the Castillo de Solís and the Mudéjar church of Nuestra Señora de la Encarnación survive. The Juanar valley, singled out for its natural beauty, is in the municipality (Andalusian tourist board). About 41 minutes by car from Casa de la Familia.

guide.summary: Parque de la Paloma: stor park med dyr og en sø, ca. 25 min i bil fra Casa de la Familia.

records.name: Parque El Esparragal
records.description: Parque El Esparragal is a public park in Urbanización Mijas Golf at Urb. Mijas Golf, 4, 29651 Las Lagunas de Mijas, Málaga. From Casa de la Familia it is about 7 minutes by car (Google route check, Saturday 10:00). According to Mijas town council (September 2021), the park is a natural space near the river with many trees, barbecue areas and benches, and a fenced children's play area with swings, a wooden play structure and a 20-metre zip line that children and adults can use (up to 137 kg). records.description: Paseo Marítimo de Fuengirola is Fuengirola's seafront promenade (Puerto Deportivo Fuengirola, Local 301, 29640 Fuengirola, Málaga, España). records.name: Playa de la Rada (Estepona)
records.description: Playa de la Rada is Estepona's main beach in the town centre, with a landscaped promenade lined with palms. Spain.info (Turespaña) lists dark sand, calm water ('aguas tranquilas'), about 2,300 m by 50 m, high occupancy, urban, easy access on foot, and services including toilets, showers, a children's area and a sports area. It is not on the 2026 Blue Flag list (no Estepona beach is). guide.summary: Playa de la Rada, Estepona: lang bystrand med roligt vand og en promenade med haveanlæg.

records.name: Playa de Nagüeles
records.description: Playa de Nagüeles lies on Marbella's Golden Mile between the town and Puerto Banús. Spain.info (Turespaña) lists golden sand, moderate waves, about 1,600 m by 40 m, high occupancy, semi-urban, easy access on foot, and services including sunbed and parasol hire, water-sports hire and showers; toilets are not listed. Blue Flag 2026 under the name Nagüeles-Casablanca. Rocks: the official sources describe a sand beach with easy access on foot, so it meets the project's beach rule (owner decision 2026-11-02). guide.summary: Playa de Nagüeles, Marbella: strand med gylden sand på Golden Mile; Blåt Flag 2026 (Nagüeles-Casablanca).

records.name: Playa de San Pedro de Alcántara

Spain.info (Turespaña) lists sand and gravel (dark), moderate waves, about 1,400 m by 35 m, high occupancy, semi-urban, easy access on foot, several restaurants and beach bars, a promenade, and services including toilets and showers. The 2026 Blue Flag list names 'San Pedro de Alcántara (Guadalmina)'; whether that covers the stretch at this point is not confirmed. records.name: Playa la Malagueta
records.description: La Malagueta is an urban beach close to Málaga's historic centre, between the port and La Caleta: about 1,200 m long and 45 m wide, medium-grain sand, with a promenade and a varied choice of places to eat along it (Málaga City Council). The council lists a lifeguard team, first-aid equipment, an accessible point, toilets and showers; spain.info adds a children's area and a sports area. Málaga runs a seasonal assisted-bathing service here, by appointment. Blue Flag 2026. Rocks: the official sources describe a sand beach with easy access on foot, so it meets the project's beach rule (owner decision 2026-11-02). About 41 minutes by car from Casa de la Familia; the Alcazaba, Gibralfaro and the Centre Pompidou are within about a kilometre (spain.info).

guide.summary: Playa de la Malagueta, Málaga: central bystrand ved havnen; Blå Flag 2026.

records.name: Playa de Puerto Banús

The Costa del Sol tourist board describes a semi-urban, golden-sand beach about 1,500 m long and 40 m wide, bordered by a long promenade (search excerpt; the page itself blocks automated reading). It is not on the 2026 Blue Flag list. Facilities and lifeguards are not checked. Rocks: the tourist board describes a sand beach with easy access on foot, so it meets the project's beach rule (owner decision 2026-11-02). About 36 minutes by car from Casa de la Familia.

guide.summary: Playa de Puerto Banús, Marbella: strand med gylden sand ved siden af lystbådehavnen og med en lang promenade.

records.name: Puerto Banús

guide.summary: Puerto Banús: Marbellas luksuriøse lystbådehavn og forlystelsesområde ved siden af stranden.

records.name: Puerto Colorado (Sierra de Mijas)
records.description: Puerto Colorado (Sierra de Mijas) is a trail area in the Sierra de Mijas (29650 Mijas, Málaga, España). From Casa de la Familia it is about 23 minutes by car (Google route check, Saturday 10:00). Puerto Colorado is the end point of a family stage of the Málaga provincial council's Gran Senda network (Sendero 07, Mijas - Puerto Colorado), which starts in Mijas village and passes the Ermita del Calvario. A 2018 Mijas council walking programme gives the route from the Via Crucis to Puerto Colorado as 7.5 km with 500 m of climb. Trail details were not yet read from the official page. Check conditions before setting out.

guide.summary: Puerto Colorado (Sierra de Mijas): område med stier i Sierra de Mijas, ca. 23 min i bil fra Casa de la Familia.

records.name: Puerto Deportivo de Estepona

It describes the food and leisure offer inside the port as high level and a regular meeting point, and mentions a traditional craft market every Sunday morning. A news item on the page says the port has 45 businesses. About 54 minutes by car from Casa de la Familia (Google route check, Saturday 10:00). Address on the site: Torre de Control, 29680 Estepona. records.name: Puerto Marina Benalmádena
records.description: Puerto Marina Benalmádena is Benalmádena's marina with shops and restaurants (Calle la Fragata, A11, 29630 Benalmádena, Málaga, España). The marina is run by a municipal company. The Sea Life aquarium is on the marina (see its own record). Check before visiting.

guide.summary: Puerto Marina Benalmádena: Benalmádenas lystbådehavn med butikker og restauranter, ca. 28 min i bil fra Casa de la Familia.

records.name: Ragazzi Pizza & Pasta
records.description: Ragazzi Pizza & Pasta is an Italian restaurant on the Paseo Marítimo Rey de España in Fuengirola. Its own website says it serves traditional pasta dishes, lasagne, cannelloni and Neapolitan pizza made with fresh sourdough. guide.summary: Ragazzi Pizza & Pasta: italiensk restaurant på Paseo Marítimo i Fuengirola med pasta og pizza, ca. 11 min i bil fra Casa de la Familia.

records.name: Restaurante Cerros del Águila
records.description: Restaurante Cerros del Águila is a bar and grill at the sports area of Urbanización Cerros del Águila at Urb. Cerros del Águila. Zona deportiva. Num 5, 29650 Mijas Costa, Málaga. From Casa de la Familia it is about 7 minutes on foot (0.48 km, Google's walking route) or about 3 minutes by car (Google route check, Saturday 10:00). records.name: Sierra de las Nieves
records.description: Sierra de las Nieves was declared Spain's 16th national park in 2021 and has been a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve since 1995, covering roughly 23,000 hectares across several municipalities including Tolox, El Burgo, Yunquera, Ronda and Parauta. As a protected mountain area rather than a single site, it has no one official entrance: the Mancomunidad de Municipios de la Sierra de las Nieves (the municipal association that runs the park's own tourism site) lists 15 separate tourist offices across the surrounding villages. This record uses the Oficina de Turismo de El Burgo (C/ Alcalde Eduardo Carbonel Cruz, s/n; Wed-Thu 09:00-15:00, Fri-Sat 10:00-14:00/16:00-18:00, Sun 09:00-13:00, closed Mon-Tue; tel. +34 658 034 452) as a representative anchor point, about 79 minutes' drive from Casa de la Familia (route-checked to El Burgo specifically — other access points such as Tolox or Yunquera would have different drive times). A new, purpose-built national-park visitor centre at 'Conejeras' was reported under construction in 2025; it is unknown whether it has opened yet. The best-known hike, to Torrecilla peak (the highest point in Málaga province), is described with conflicting distance figures across sources (roughly 10-14 km round trip depending on the source and starting point) and its permit requirements were not confirmed in this research — only a separate trail (the Yunquera stone-pine/pinsapar loop) was confirmed to need advance online authorization. Dogs-allowed policy and visitor-centre facilities are unverified.

guide.summary: Sierra de las Nieves er en nationalpark (udpeget 2021) og UNESCO-biosfærereservat i bjergene mellem Tolox, Ronda, El Burgo og Yunquera; den har 15 separate kommunale turistkontorer og intet samlet besøgssted, og tilladelser til stier og faciliteter er stort set ikke bekræftet.

records.name: Tarifa
records.description: Tarifa sits at Spain's southern tip facing the Strait of Gibraltar, about 1 hour 50 minutes' drive from Casa de la Familia (Google Maps main figure). Its Castillo de Guzmán el Bueno, a 10th-century fortress built under Caliph Abderramán III of Córdoba, overlooks the port and the strait toward Morocco. The castle's official website gives current opening hours (closed Monday and Tuesday; Wednesday to Sunday 10:00-16:00, last entry 15:15) and admission prices from €2-5 per person depending on the ticket (castle, castle plus Adarve walkway, or Adarve only), with reduced rates for students and children. The old town has three notable churches built partly over former mosques (San Mateo, San Francisco de Asís, Santa María). The town is consistently described across independent sources as a major kitesurfing and windsurfing destination because of the strong, near-constant 'levante' wind. Tarifa neighbours Duna de Bolonia and Baelo Claudia, both separate existing records, along the coast road toward Cádiz. Castle accessibility and parking have not been confirmed from an official source.

records.name: Tolox
records.description: Tolox sits at the foot of the Sierra de las Nieves, about 56 minutes' drive from Casa de la Familia (OSRM route check; not yet re-measured in Google Maps). The town's wellness draw is the Balneario de Tolox, also known as Fuente Amargosa: a thermal spa whose hypothermal, naturally gas-bearing waters were discovered in 1867 and have been used since 1869 for respiratory-condition treatments taken by inhalation; the current building dates to 1930, rebuilt after a major 1906 flood destroyed the original. Its own website states it is open only from 1 June to 16 October each year, not year-round — this directly resolves the open editorial question about Tolox's wellness offering, but also means any visit must be timed to that window; the spa was closed for the winter when re-checked on 29 October 2026, and the 2027 dates are not yet published. Owner decision 2026-10-29: Tolox is kept and marked as a seasonal place (June-October). Daily hours, current treatment prices, whether day visitors (not staying at the spa) can use the facilities, and the historic town centre's own sights have not yet been confirmed from an official source.

guide.summary: Tolox er en lille hvid kurby i Málaga-provinsen; det historiske Balneario de Tolox (Fuente Amargosa) er et dokumenteret termalbad, men det har kun åbent i sæsonen (1. juni-16. oktober), ikke hele året.

records.name: Vejer de la Frontera
records.description: Vejer de la Frontera is a hilltop white town in Cádiz province, about 2 hours 20 minutes' drive from Casa de la Familia (Google Maps main figure). Its Castillo de Vejer dates to the 10th-11th century, was once home to the Dukes of Medina Sidonia, and was declared a Historic-Artistic Monument (Bien de Interés Cultural) in 1931. Sources on the castle's current opening hours and admission price actively conflict: one account describes opening hours as historically 'erratic' with visitors advised to ask the tourist office; another claims a specific seasonal schedule and a small entrance fee; others describe free admission. None of these could be confirmed against an official ayuntamiento or tourist-office source in this research pass, so no hours or price are published here. The town's general character (narrow hilltop streets, views over the surrounding countryside toward the coast) is well attested across sources but has not been itemised into specific sourced facts yet.

guide.summary: Vejer de la Frontera er en hvid bjergby i Cádiz-provinsen med en borg fra 900-1000-tallet på toppen, engang hjemsted for hertugerne af Medina Sidonia; åbningstider og priser er ikke bekræftet og stemmer ikke overens på tværs af de fundne kilder.

records.name: Zero Latency Miramar
records.description: Zero Latency Miramar is a free-roam virtual-reality arena at the Miramar shopping centre at Av. de la Encarnación, s/n, 29640 Fuengirola, Málaga. From Casa de la Familia it is about 9 minutes by car (Google route check, Saturday 10:00). The operator's pages (checked 2026-11-02): an arena of more than 200 m² where up to eight players move freely without cables; standard hours Monday-Thursday 15:00-22:00, Friday 13:00-23:00, Saturday 12:00-23:00 and Sunday 12:00-22:00 (the operator notes these may differ on the day). Games last 15-30 minutes, with packages of 45-60 minutes. There is no fixed minimum age, but each game has a minimum height (Málaga page), and the operator general FAQ recommends players be 13 or older (some venues differ); call the venue on +34 951 811 105 before bringing children (owner decision 2026-11-11). The FAQ also says the games are generally not suitable for pregnant players, people who need mobility assistance, who are deaf or blind, or who have heart conditions, and that VR can trigger seizures. On its own booking site a gift voucher for one ticket costs €29.95 (eight tickets €239.60); games are booked online, staff speak Spanish and English (own Facebook page; phone +34 951 81 11 05), and groups of more than eight should book by e-mail (info_malaga@zerolatencyvr.es) or Instagram (@zerolatencymalaga). Check with the venue before visiting.

guide.summary: Zero Latency Miramar: virtual reality-arena med fri bevægelse i Miramar-indkøbscentret, ca. 9 min i bil fra Casa de la Familia.
